topic_tag: a composer's use of a folk tune in a symphony
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Comparing the symphony with the village version, one critic observed that the composer had ______ the tune.

worlds.passage: In 1907 a composer built one movement of his first symphony on a folk tune he had heard in a fishing village. In the village a single fiddler played it, with nothing beneath it. In the symphony the violins play it note for note from start to finish while the cellos play the village's wedding song at the same time. Each tune's high notes fall where the other's low notes are, so that a listener can follow either one the whole way through. Comparing the symphony with the village version, one critic observed that the composer had ______ the tune.
worlds.explanation: A tune once played alone now runs together with a second tune, the two fitted so each stays clear against the other, so the composer "braided" the tune. "Clipped" fails because it is played from start to finish; "animated" fails because the change is a second line joined to it, not a livelier pace; "cleansed" fails because it is kept note for note.

clipped.why: The whole tune is played, so none of it is cut off.

animated.why: The change is the fitting of a second melody to it, not a quicker or livelier rhythm.

cleansed.why: The tune's own notes are untouched, so nothing in it was removed as rough.

worlds.passage: In 1907 a composer built one movement of his first symphony on a folk tune he had heard in a fishing village. The village fiddlers played it as thirty-two bars, repeated for as long as the dancing lasted, and its first eight bars were the part every child in the village could hum. In the symphony the orchestra plays the phrase the children knew, note for note and at the fiddlers' own speed, over and over until the movement ends. Comparing the symphony with the village version, one critic observed that the composer had ______ the tune.
worlds.explanation: The phrase the children knew is the tune's first eight bars of thirty-two, and the symphony repeats that phrase alone to the end, so the composer "clipped" the tune: he cut it short. "Braided" fails because nothing else is joined to it; the movement just repeats the phrase; "animated" fails because it keeps the fiddlers' own speed; "cleansed" fails because the phrase keeps every note.

braided.quote: over and over until the movement ends
braided.why: The movement repeats the one fragment; no second line is combined with it.

animated.why: Its pace is unchanged, so it was not made livelier.

cleansed.why: What remains is exactly the village notes; the change is in length only.

worlds.passage: In 1907 a composer built one movement of his first symphony on a folk tune he had heard in a fishing village. The village fiddlers played it with sliding notes, a sharpened fourth, and a rough drone, all of which the composer's teachers had taught him to call errors. In the symphony the tune keeps its full length and its speed; every slide is gone, the fourth sits back in the ordinary scale, and smooth chords stand where the drone was. Comparing the symphony with the village version, one critic observed that the composer had ______ the tune.
worlds.explanation: Everything his training counted as an error is taken out, leaving the tune smooth and regular, so the composer "cleansed" the tune. "Clipped" fails because it keeps its full length; "braided" fails because the chords replace the drone as harmony, not as a second tune woven with it; "animated" fails because its speed is unchanged.

clipped.why: Nothing is cut from the tune's length; only its rough features are removed.

braided.quote: smooth chords stand where the drone was
braided.why: The chords are accompaniment replacing the drone, not a second melody interwoven with the tune.

animated.why: The changes remove what he was trained to see as faults; they give the tune no new liveliness.

worlds.passage: In 1907 a composer built one movement of his first symphony on a folk tune he had heard in a fishing village. In the village it was a slow lament, sung at funerals with each note held long. The composer kept every note and gave the tune to the full orchestra at twice the speed, over a quick, skipping rhythm in the drums, so that audiences at the premiere tapped their feet to it. Comparing the symphony with the village version, one critic observed that the composer had ______ the tune.
worlds.explanation: A slow funeral lament becomes quick and dancing, enough to set feet tapping, so the composer "animated" the tune. "Clipped" fails because every note is kept; "braided" fails because the drums supply a rhythm, not a second tune woven with it; "cleansed" fails because nothing is removed as a fault; the notes stay and only the pace and rhythm change.

clipped.why: No part of the tune is cut off.

braided.why: The added part is a rhythm beneath the tune, not another melody interwoven with it.

cleansed.why: The change is from mournful to lively; nothing rough in the tune is stripped out.
